_comment: The block manifest consumed by `klt signoff --manifest` (klayout-tools#722,
Phase 0 of epic #706). This file -- not a prose checklist -- is this block's
VERDICT OF RECORD for its gap to T1, and it is what the fleet tier roll-up
(2AMLogic/2am#956) consumes to grade this block's row mechanically. See
signoff/README.md for the full claim and docs/t1-gap.md for the in-repo map.
FIELDS
block   required. Identifies this block's row in the fleet roll-up, which
consumes exactly this value.
kind    required, and confirmed against the block rather than taken from
the issue that asked for this file. `mixed-signal`: the design
genuinely partitions, in one repo, into a transistor-level analog
signal path and a sky130_fd_sc_hd standard-cell digital section
that is placed and routed by OpenROAD (`klt place-and-route`), not
hand-drawn. See `partition_boundary` below and signoff/README.md's
'Why mixed-signal' section. A mixed-signal manifest renders every
T1 item TWICE (once per partition, 22 rows) and must satisfy both
columns of the per-kind items, one per partition.
evidence  item id -> evidence entry. A bare `"<id>"` key cites the same
evidence for both partitions' rows; a `"<id>.<analog|digital>"`
key grades only that partition. Both forms are used deliberately
below -- see the per-item notes.
WHAT IS CITED, AND WHY EACH CITATION IS HONEST (against this tree)
3   (bare -- both partitions) layout/sar-adc-top/.../drc.json. `klt drc`
ran on sar_adc_top.gds, the COMPOSED top-level stream, which contains
both partitions' drawn geometry (cdac_array + sampling_frontend +
comparator on the analog side, sar_sequencer + seln_inverters on the
digital side -- see that report's compose.request.json). So one clean
DRC genuinely covers both partitions and the bare key is not a
shortcut. status: clean, and the pin below is the sha256 of the
committed sar_adc_top.gds (verified; see check-evidence-hashes.py).
THE COVERAGE GAPS ARE NOT GRADED: `klt signoff` renders item 3 `met`
on `status: "clean"` alone. This block's deck leaves 22 drawn
layer/datatype pairs rule-free and skips 5 rules; both lists are
enumerated in signoff/README.md, which is where the item's
claimant-enforced disclosure obligation is actually discharged.
4   (bare -- both partitions) layout/sar-adc-top/.../lvs.json. Cited even
though it does NOT pass: `status: "mismatch"` (98 mismatches), so it
renders unmet/check_failed. That is the point -- 'an LVS run exists
and did not match' is a materially different, and more useful,
machine-readable statement than 'no evidence'. NOT PINNED, and the
omission is deliberate rather than an oversight: this envelope was
produced by klt 0.5.0, whose `klt lvs` writes `provenance.input:
null`, so there is no envelope-side hash for a manifest pin to match
and a pin here would be decorative (and, because check_failed is
evaluated first, never even consulted). The freshness axis is carried
instead by the envelope's own environment.layout_sha256 /
environment.reference_sha256, which check-evidence-hashes.py
re-derives from the committed netlists on every push.
8.analog  signoff/evidence/characterization-report.generic.json, a generic
envelope (the only kind item 8 accepts) wrapping
docs/characterization-report.md. PARTITION-QUALIFIED on purpose: that
report covers spec/target-spec.md's Target table, which is the ADC's
analog/system-level spec. The doc's item 8 additionally requires Fmax,
area and power across the corner set for a digital partition, and this
repo has none of those, so `8.digital` is left uncited and renders
unmet/no_evidence rather than borrowing the analog row's pass.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CITED (against this tree, 2026-09-23)
1, 2, 9, 10  no `klt` verb backs these; `klt signoff` grades them on
'some passing envelope was cited', not on topical relevance
(klayout-tools signoff.md, 'Items 1, 2, 9, and 10'). Every one of the
four has real work behind it in this repo -- committed xschem sources
with a CI-gated netlist regeneration check (1), reproducibly generated
GDS with per-flow records (2), a per-spec-row testbench index gated by
sim/check_spec_coverage.py (9), README + license + CI (10) -- and
NONE of it is a klt envelope. Citing an unrelated passing envelope to
turn those rows green is precisely the dishonesty this manifest exists
to prevent, so they render unmet/no_evidence and signoff/README.md
states what actually stands behind each.
5   no `klt sim` envelope exists: sim/ campaigns mint this repo's own
Markdown evidence records, not `klt sim` JSON. And the spec half of
the item is not met either -- spec/target-spec.md's sample-rate and
ENOB/INL-DNL target rows are still DRAFT.
6   two `klt yield` envelopes DO exist (sim/cdac-array-transfer/ and
sim/enob-estimate/yield-reports/), and both report status: "fail".
Neither is cited, for two reasons that are about the citation, not
about the campaign: (a) each names its samples document as a
/tmp/tmp*.json path that no longer exists, so `klt signoff` cannot
hash it and the item can never be freshness-pinned; (b) the item's two
statistical spec rows (ENOB, INL/DNL) are split across the two
reports and only one entry per item is accepted, so citing either one
alone would misrepresent the coverage. signoff/README.md records both
verdicts in full instead.
7   no `klt pex` report exists. Item 7 accepts nothing else -- a clean DRC
or a pre-layout sim renders wrong_kind by design.
11  (bare -- both partitions) a COMPOUND citation, the only item whose
entry may be an array: the `klt erc` supply run plus the LVS report
item 4 grades, which is what this item's own grading path
(`_grade_power_delivery`) requires. Both name the same composed GDS
by hash, so one verdict is not smuggled in against another revision.
Cited even though the item does NOT render met, for exactly item 4's
reason: `unmet`/`check_failed` -- 'the ERC ran, the LVS ran, and the
pair does not yet clear this item' -- is a materially more useful
machine-readable statement than `no_evidence`.
WHY IT DOES NOT RENDER MET, and neither half of this is hidden:
(a) the supply-continuity half PASSES. The cited run reports
erc_status `clean`, zero findings: all four declared supplies
(VDD, GND, VPWR, VGND) resolve to exactly one electrical island
each, no erc.unconnected_net and no erc.supply_short. That is
new as of issue #355 (DR-010), which tied both standard-cell
macros' met5 PDN straps together and out to two new top-level
supply pins; #344's first run had VPWR and VGND each splitting
into two islands that reached no top-level supply.
(b) the REASON OF RECORD is item 4's LVS, not the continuity half.
`_grade_power_delivery` resolves the cited LVS part and tests
it BEFORE it looks at the supply spec, so that report's
`mismatch` status (klayout-tools#1878) short-circuits grading
at `check_failed` -- which is why the rendered reason is not
about (a) at all.
(c) a SECOND, LATENT reason sits behind it, reached once (b)
clears: the item ALSO requires zero `erc.missing_tie` from a
tie the run actually checked, and this spec declares no
`ties[]` at all -- disclosed in-report as ties_disclosure.kind
'tool_limitation' (klayout-tools#2169 turns a correct ties[]
declaration on a routed standard-cell design into a FALSE
erc.supply_short). The grader has a distinct reason for exactly
that state (supply_spec_disclosed_tool_limitation), and it is
not a pass either. So clearing the LVS alone would move the
reason, not the verdict.
So: better evidence than before, and NOT a met row. docs/t1-gap.md's
item-11 line says the same thing in prose, and signoff/README.md's
table carries the per-supply detail.
REGENERATING / CHECKING
bash signoff/run-signoff.sh            # rewrite signoff/t1-report.json
bash signoff/run-signoff.sh --check    # fail if the committed report drifted
CI runs the --check form on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/
ci.yml, job `signoff-check`), so a manifest citing an artifact that has since
changed turns the build red rather than rotting quietly.
This `_comment` key is not part of the manifest schema; `klt signoff` reads
only block/kind/partition_boundary/evidence, so editing this block alone
re-renders t1-report.json byte-identically.

partition_boundary.analog: The transistor-level signal path, as instantiated in design/sar_adc_top.sch: the bootstrapped sampling front end (xfe, .subckt sampling_frontend), the differential charge-redistribution CDAC array (xcdac, .subckt cdac_array), the StrongARM-class comparator (xcmp, .subckt comparator), and the top-level half-LSB offset-injection network of DR-009 (XChoff_p/XChoff_n cap_mim_m3_1 plus the XMoff_* pfet_01v8/nfet_01v8 switches). Nets: VINP, VINN, VCM, VREFP, VREFN, TOP_P, TOP_N, BOT_OFF_P, BOT_OFF_N, BPREF_P_NC, BPREF_N_NC. Layout cells: cdac_array, sampling_frontend, comparator (layout/cdac-array/, layout/sampling-frontend/, layout/comparator/, composed into layout/sar-adc-top/).
partition_boundary.digital: The sky130_fd_sc_hd standard-cell logic, placed and routed by OpenROAD via `klt place-and-route`: the (N+1)-stage walking-one ring sequencer and 10-bit SAR register (xseq, .subckt sar_sequencer) and the top-level standard-cell bank laid out as seln_inverters (the xand_seln*/xand_selp* SELn/SELp drivers, xinv_clkcap, xinv_dout9n, the xxor_code* offset-binary recoding stage of DR-008, and the xand_halflsb/xinv_halflsb enable pair of DR-009). Nets: CLK, RST_B, COMP_OUT, DOUT9..DOUT0, PH_B9..PH_B0, PH_EOC, PH_SAMPLE/SAMPLE_INT, BUSY, SELp8..SELp0, SELn8..SELn0, ADCOUT8..ADCOUT0, DOUT9N, HALF_LSB_EN, HALF_LSB_ENN, VPWR, VGND. Layout cells: sar_sequencer, seln_inverters (layout/sar-sequencer/, layout/seln-inverters/, composed into layout/sar-adc-top/). Crossings (a boundary is only reviewable if its crossings are named) -- analog to digital: comparator.OUTP drives COMP_OUT into xseq. Digital to analog: SELn8..0/SELp8..0 drive the CDAC bottom plates, HALF_LSB_EN/HALF_LSB_ENN drive the DR-009 offset network, SAMPLE_INT (the sequencer's PH_SAMPLE) drives the sampling front end, and CLKN (xinv_clkcap) drives the comparator clock. The supplies are NOT shared across the boundary in the netlist -- the analog side is on VDD/GND and the standard cells on VPWR/VGND -- which is an item-11 question (issue #344), not an item-4 one.
